examples.title: Build only SER part cards
examples.situation: A generic drawing has a wheel between transmission and blades; a manufacturer sheet marks a front wheel for DE/DER only.
reasoning: Select SER-applicable handlebar-height adjuster, engine/controls, belt cover/clutch, transmission/shift, rotary, drag bars and air cleaner from the manual.
Use a simple engine → belt-tension clutch → transmission/rotary explanation, marking it a functional teaching path rather than an exposed diagram of a gearbox.
Reject the DE/DER-only front wheel, generic centrifugal cylinders and unsupported material/power labels.
examples.takeaway: A model-labelled, checkable part board; no invented part.

examples.title: One acre is a site question, not a feddan
examples.situation: A farmer has one acre with tight rows and asks for hand or machine weeding.
reasoning: Convert one acre to about 4,047 m² or 0.964 Egyptian feddan; do not use 4–6 hours as a conversion.
Measure row clearance/stone risk and compare actual labour, time, machine fit and safety.
If actual fuel use and job-time data are missing, leave operating cost blank pending measurement.
examples.takeaway: Conditional choice with dimensions and missing data, not an automatic machine recommendation.

examples.title: Quote a service only from valid inputs
examples.situation: A learner proposes a weeding service for neighbouring small plots.
reasoning: List actual total working area and suitable rows, setup/travel time, labour and maintenance.
Distinguish manufacturer 2.4 L capacity from measured L/hour and source 2.3 L/hour not verified for SER.
Request local fuel and labour prices and reserve for breakdown, safety and transport before a price or margin.
examples.takeaway: A transparent calculation template; no invented cost or guaranteed profit.
